context:
Goal: CI runs start within a few minutes, so a ready pull request merges on the day it is handed in.
Problem (money): a started CI job waits a median 21.7 minutes in the queue (p90 38.2, max 69.0), and a ready pull request waited 69 to 174 minutes from its ready mark to merge today; fixing it by capacity costs money or cuts CI coverage, so only you can pick.
Based on (measured): batch runner 10's read of 9 checks runs, 14:53 CST: 208 started jobs; Windows jobs wait a median 28.4 min (67 jobs), Ubuntu jobs 12.9 (141 jobs); about 12 heavy runs an hour of 214 to 504 runner-minutes each; at most 36 jobs ran at once, so the cap is at least 36 (its value is unmeasured). Not re-measured by triage.
Departs from: main — every pull request run starts 33 to 35 jobs, 13 of them on Windows, and no record names a capacity or concurrency limit — this question adds a capacity choice.
Waiting on: nothing is stopped; a read-only measure of the draft-run share and of whether other repos share the runners is running now; batch runner 10 reads your answer.

options.gain: No money or CI coverage is spent on a guess.
options.how: A read-only measure of the draft-run share and of whether other repos share the runners finishes; then batch runner 10 asks you again.
options.label: Measure first, then ask again (recommended)
options.lose: The queue stays as it is for a few more hours.

options.how: The account moves CI jobs to larger paid runners.
options.label: Pay for larger runners

options.gain: One repo cannot starve the others.
options.how: One repo can run only so many jobs at once.
options.label: Cap concurrent jobs per repo
options.lose: This repo's own runs queue longer at peak.

options.gain: The longest waiters (Windows jobs wait a median 28.4 min) go away.
options.how: A pull request run drops some of its 13 Windows jobs.
options.label: Run fewer Windows jobs on each pull request run
options.lose: Less Windows test coverage on each pull request run.

options.gain: No spend and no lost coverage.
options.label: No change
options.lose: Ready pull requests keep waiting 1 to 3 hours to merge.

ref: batch runner 10 message 15:05 CST Nov 18, consultant approved 15:04 CST

shown.label: Run fewer Windows jobs on each pull request run

title: A started CI job waits a median 21.7 minutes in the queue: spend money, cut coverage, or measure more first?
why: a spends nothing until the draft-run share and the runner sharing are known; b to d each cost money or coverage on a guess. Recommended by batch runner 10, not owner-typed.
